tool.name: Bambu
tool.description: transcript discovery and quantification from long-read RNA-seq

param.name: ndr
param.label: Novel discovery rate (NDR) threshold
param.help: Leave empty to let Bambu choose it from the data (recommended)

param.name: min_read_count
param.label: Minimum read count for a novel transcript
param.help: Reads a novel read class needs within one sample (opt.discovery min.readCount)

param.name: min_sample_number
param.label: Minimum number of samples reaching that count
param.help: Samples that must reach the minimum read count (opt.discovery min.sampleNumber). Above the number of input BAMs, nothing novel is kept.

#import re ## Sample names become count-table column headers, so keep them to safe characters and unique #set $sample_names = [] #for $bam in $reads #set $name = re.sub(r'\.bam$', '', str($bam.element_identifier)) #set $name = re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9_\-]', '_', $name) or 'sample' #set $candidate = $name #set $n = 2 ## rn, TXNAME and GENEID are column names in Bambu's own tables #while $candidate in $sample_names or $candidate in ('rn', 'TXNAME', 'GENEID') #set $candidate = '%s_%d' % ($name, $n) #set $n += 1 #end while #silent $sample_names.append($candidate) #end for suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(bambu))
ncore <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("GALAXY_SLOTS", "1")) #set $names_r = ', '.join(['"%s"' % $s for $s in $sample_names]) sample_names <- c($names_r) ## Bambu names each sample after its BAM file and uses that name in more than one table, ## so give it the files under their final names instead of renaming columns afterwards dir.create("named") reads <- file.path("named", paste0(sample_names, ".bam")) stopifnot(file.rename(sprintf("bams/input_%d.bam", seq_along(sample_names) - 1L), reads))
## cached genomes come with an index; only build one when there is none if (!file.exists("genome.fa.fai")) Rsamtools::indexFa("genome.fa") ## a character genome is first looked up as a BSgenome name, which needs network access genome <- Rsamtools::FaFile("genome.fa") annotations <- prepareAnnotations("annotation.gtf")
#if $analysis.mode == 'quant': discovery <- FALSE ndr <- NULL opt_discovery <- NULL #else: discovery <- TRUE #if str($analysis.ndr): ndr <- $analysis.ndr #else: ndr <- NULL #end if opt_discovery <- list(min.readCount = $analysis.min_read_count, min.sampleNumber = $analysis.min_sample_number) #end if
result <- bambu( reads = reads, annotations = annotations, genome = genome, NDR = ndr, opt.discovery = opt_discovery, discovery = discovery, quant = #if $analysis.mode == 'discovery' then 'FALSE' else 'TRUE'#, stranded = $stranded, ncore = ncore, verbose = TRUE )
#if $analysis.mode == 'discovery': ## without quantification bambu returns only the extended annotation dir.create("output") writeToGTF(result, "output/extended_annotations.gtf") #else: writeBambuOutput(result, path = "output") #end if

param.name: reads
param.label: Long-read alignments
param.help: One BAM per sample, from minimap2 in spliced mode (-ax splice). Sample names are taken from the dataset or collection element names.

param.name: source
param.label: Reference genome
param.option: Use a genome from the history

param.name: genome
param.label: Genome (FASTA)
param.help: The genome the reads were aligned to

param.name: annotation
param.label: Reference annotation (GTF)
param.help: Chromosome names must match the genome and the alignments

param.name: stranded
param.label: Stranded reads?
param.help: Enable for direct RNA or stranded cDNA protocols, where the read strand is the transcript strand. Leave off for standard cDNA, whose reads come from either strand.

tool.help:
## What it does
Bambu discovers and quantifies transcripts from long-read RNA-seq (Oxford Nanopore or PacBio). It groups spliced read alignments into *read classes* that share the same intron chain, scores read classes that do not match the reference annotation with a model trained on the annotated ones, and adds the high-confidence candidates to the annotation as novel transcripts. It then estimates the expression of every known and novel transcript with an EM algorithm.
This wrapper runs `prepareAnnotations`, `bambu` and `writeBambuOutput` from the [Bioconductor package](https://bioconductor.org/packages/bambu), the same steps as the nf-core/nanoseq pipeline. In discovery-only mode there are no counts to write, so it calls `writeToGTF` instead of `writeBambuOutput`.
## Input
- One or more **BAM** files of long reads aligned to the genome with a spliced aligner such as minimap2 (`-ax splice`, or `-ax splice -uf -k14` for direct RNA). Give one BAM per sample; a collection works. - The **reference genome** the reads were aligned to. - The reference **annotation** in GTF format, with chromosome names matching the genome.
Two kinds of GTF give wrong results without an error in Bambu 3.12.1:
- A GTF with other attributes that end in `gene_id` or `transcript_id`, such as StringTie's `ref_gene_id` or NCBI's `orig_transcript_id`. Bambu can read those instead of the real IDs; remove them first. - An extended annotation written by an earlier Bambu run. Numbering of novel transcripts starts again at `BambuTx1`, so new and old novel transcripts can share an ID.
### Sample names
The sample columns of the count tables are named after the datasets or collection elements:
- a trailing `.bam` is removed; - every character other than a letter, a digit, `_` or `-` is replaced by `_`; - names that end up the same (`s.1` and `s_1`, or the same dataset given twice) get `_2`, `_3` and so on appended, in input order.
## Options
- **Analysis**: discovery plus quantification (the default, as nf-core/nanoseq runs it), quantification of the annotated transcripts only, or discovery only, which writes the extended annotation without counts. - **Novel discovery rate (NDR)**: the maximum expected fraction of novel transcripts among those kept, between 0 and 1. Leave it empty to let Bambu pick a threshold from the data, which is the recommended setting; it then reports the value it chose in the job's standard error. Use a lower value for a well-annotated genome and a higher one for a poorly annotated organism. - **Minimum read count**: a novel read class needs at least this many reads *within a sample* to count for that sample; reads are not summed across samples (Bambu's `min.readCount`). The same threshold decides which read classes Bambu scores and trains its model on. - **Minimum number of samples**: how many samples must reach the minimum read count (`min.sampleNumber`). A value above the number of input BAMs keeps no novel transcripts. - **Stranded reads**: turn on for direct RNA and other stranded protocols.
## Output
With discovery on (every mode except quantification only):
- **Extended annotation** (GTF): the reference annotation plus the novel transcripts.
With quantification on (every mode except discovery only):
- **Transcript counts**: the estimated number of reads per transcript and sample. - **Transcript CPM**: the same estimates as counts per million. - **Full-length transcript counts**: reads that cover the full intron chain of the transcript. - **Unique transcript counts**: reads compatible with only that transcript. - **Gene counts**: reads per gene. This is the sum of the transcript counts plus the reads that fall in the gene but are not compatible with any of its transcripts, so it can be larger than the sum of the transcript rows.
Novel transcripts are named `BambuTx1`, `BambuTx2` and so on. Those in unannotated loci get the gene IDs `BambuGene1` and so on.
The count tables have one row per transcript (with its gene) or per gene, and one column per sample.
